# Abstract {.unnumbered} 

## Background

Severe pain following tonsillectomy is common and contributes to delayed discharge and secondary complications. The optimal intraoperative opioid strategy remains unknown. We evaluated variation in perioperative analgesia and its association with postoperative outcomes at a high-volume surgical centre.

## Methods

This retrospective electronic patient record cohort study included all patients undergoing tonsillectomy, adenoidectomy or adenotonsillectomy over 7 years. Patients were grouped by receipt of simple analgesia (paracetamol, dexamethasone and diclofenac) alone or with morphine, fentanyl or both. Analgesic exposure was described, and multilevel models assessed associations with rescue opioid use, recovery time and same-day discharge.

## Results

Of `r comma(nrow(df))` patients, `r N(df$adult == 0)` (`r P(df$adult == 0)`) were paediatric. Complete simple analgesia was given to `r P(adults$simple_analgesia_given)` of adults and `r P(paeds$simple_analgesia_given)` of children; `r P(adults$intra_op_opioid_given)` (n = `r N(adults$intra_op_opioid_given)`) and `r P(paeds$intra_op_opioid_given)` (n = `r N(paeds$intra_op_opioid_given)`), respectively, received an intraoperative strong opioid. Children predominantly received fentanyl alone, whereas adult strategies varied substantially. In adults, rescue opioid use did not differ significantly between groups after adjustment, but combined morphine and fentanyl was associated with shorter recovery time (`r beta(3, "treatment_arm4")` minutes, 95% CI `r beta(3, "treatment_arm4", "conf.low")` to `r beta(3, "treatment_arm4", "conf.high")`).

## Conclusions

Intraoperative opioid strategies varied in adults but were more homogeneous in children. After adjustment for patient, surgical and anaesthetic factors, combined fentanyl and morphine with simple analgesia was associated with shorter recovery time, without a significant difference in rescue opioid use. Further work addressing data quality and causality is needed to define optimal intraoperative opioid strategies.
